results.title: Exploding & Vanishing Gradient Problem in Deep Learning | Towards Data Science
results.content: **Activation Functions & Non-Linearity: Neural Networks 101**. For example, for the ***ReLU*** (rectified linear unit) activation function, the normal distribution variance needs to be initialised using \_**1/n\_in.**\_. For most industry standard neural networks, the sigmoid activation function has largely been abandoned and replaced with the ReLU as it doesn’t saturate for large positive values (it’s also more compute efficient):. Using Glorot initialisation and the ReLU (and variants) activation function helps curtail the chance of vanishing/exploding gradients at the beginning of the algorithm, but doesn’t help during training. Batch normalisation has been shown to improve the training of deep neural networks and reduce the impact of the vanishing gradients problem. Vanishing and exploding gradients occur due to the variance change between neural network layers and gradients decreasing due to the multiplication effect as they are backpropagated. In this post, we discussed three methods to reduce the chance of this effect: better activation functions, batch normalisation, and gradient clipping.

Title: Softplus returning negative values in training loop - reinforcement-learning - PyTorch Forums
# Softplus returning negative values in training loop. I’m using (torch.nn.functional.softplus(x) + 1e-6) to compute the variance that is trained in a policy gradient network. It occasionally throws a negative value which crashes the Normal(mean,variance) distribution creation for the error function. When I try and detect it and then print out the offending input, and run the same function outside of the loop, I get a different (valid) output for the same input. I’ve been fighting this for 3 days - even using different softplus approximations like a manual squareplus function, and even clamping gradients to small values, and cannot figure out what’s going on. What could be going on in the training loop that might corrupt the final model output? def __init__(self, in_features, out_dims, hidden_size=128, xrange=[0.0,1.0],min_variance=1e-6):. self.min_var = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(out_dims, requires_grad=False) + min_variance). self.range_min = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(out_dims, requires_grad=False) + xrange[0]). self.range_size = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(out_dims, requires_grad=False) + (xrange[1] - xrange[0])). self.fc1 = nn.Linear(in_features, hidden_size). self.fc2 = nn.Linear(hidden_size, hidden_size). self.fc_mu = nn.Linear(hidden_size, out_dims). self.fc_var = nn.Linear(hidden_size, out_dims). x = torch.tensor(x).float().to(device). x = F.mish(self.fc1(x)). x = F.mish(self.fc2(x)). mu = F.sigmoid(self.fc_mu(x)) * self.range_size + self.range_min. v = F.softplus(self.fc_var(x)) + self.min_var. print("softplus input",self.fc_var(x)). And here’s where it prints the detected bad value immediately before the crash:. `softplus input tensor(, device='cuda:0'). gp variance: tensor(, device='cuda:0')`. Of course, when you manually run that input through softplus:. `print(F.softplus(torch.tensor(-3.7529)))`. You get a positive output: tensor(0.0232). Is there a reason you make the min variance a param? In general I would put it as a buffer. Can you check that it’s value is unchanged? It’s just a parameter for convenience during development. I’m starting to think the problem is in the mu network since they share 2 layers and the output is a sigmoid, which could cause underflow in the gradients. **`self.min_var = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(out_dims, requires_grad=False) + min_variance)`**. `self.min_var = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(out_dims, requires_grad=False) + min_variance)`. Passes a tensor into the nn.Parameter function without a gradient… but the nn.Parameter function defaults to using a gradient anyway. The function call should be:. **`self.min_var = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(out_dims) + min_variance, requires_grad=False)`**. `self.min_var = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(out_dims) + min_variance, requires_grad=False)`. So that the parameter itself gets the no-grad parameter. I would register a buffer instead :wink:.

# Noisy gradients occurring during training. I am encountering a problem while training a pretty simple neural network where each layer is a triangular matrix weight matrix (alternating between lower and upper) and a SoftPlus activation applied at every layer, except the last layer. I was trying to see how the sum of the squares of each weight matrix gradient was varying over the number of iterations of training, and it was found to be pretty noisy with a large variance. I was suspecting vanishing or exploding gradients so I used some solutions like gradient clipping using grad\_clip\_norm\_ and grad\_clip\_value\_ but of no use. Also, I used batch normalization to solve the problem but get more noisy gradients. Any suggestions would be appreciated. Probably we’ll need more information about what you’re trying to achieve. Can you reproduce the problem in code? I am trying to implement a model for prob.density estimation that is going to map a particular distribution into normal distribution. So my loss is somewhat a negative log-likelihood function which I am trying to minimize. results.title: Understanding Weight Initialization to Prevent Vanishing and Exploding ...
results.content: Published Time: 2025-04-20T00:32:05+00:00 Understanding Weight Initialization to Prevent Vanishing and Exploding Gradients – Your Gateway to Data Mastery Your Gateway to Data Mastery #### Learn, explore, and innovate with data science. Understanding Weight Initialization to Prevent Vanishing and Exploding Gradients Date: April 19, 2025Author: Jenny Eum0 Comments When training deep neural networks, one of the challenges that often arises is the **vanishing** or **exploding gradients** problem. If the weights are poorly initialized, the gradients either **diminish** (vanish) as they pass through the layers or **grow exponentially** (explode), making training very difficult. A good strategy is to set the variance of the weight initialization based on the number of input features. * For a single neuron, one effective strategy is to **initialize the weights with a variance of 1/n​**, where n is the number of input features. This works better because ReLU has **zero gradient** for negative inputs, so initializing with a larger variance helps ensure the weights don’t become too small to learn effectively. Each layer’s weights are initialized based on the number of **inputs** to that layer. * **For each layer l**, if the number of neurons in layer l−1 (previous layer) is n(l−1), then we initialize the weights with the variance 2/n(l−1) for **ReLU** activation. **Prevents Exploding Gradients**: If weights are initialized with a large variance, the gradients during backpropagation could become very large and cause the network to **explode**. 2. **Prevents Vanishing Gradients**: If weights are initialized too small, the gradients will become **tiny** during backpropagation, causing the model to stop learning. These strategies reduce the likelihood of **vanishing or exploding gradients** by ensuring the weights are properly scaled, which makes training deep networks more stable and efficient.

  Exploding Diffusion Models
## [论文评述] Unified Directly Denoising for Both Variance Preserving and Variance Exploding Diffusion Models. # [论文评述] Unified Directly Denoising for Both Variance Preserving and Variance Exploding Diffusion Models. 这篇论文提出了一种名为 "uDDDM" (Unified Directly Denoising Diffusion Models, 统一直接去噪扩散模型) 的新型扩散模型框架。 该框架旨在统一处理两种主要的扩散模型变体：方差保持 (Variance Preserving, VP) 和方差爆炸 (Variance Exploding, VE) 的情形。 之前的 Directly Denoising Diffusion Models (DDDM) 在 VP 场景下展现了单步生成高质量图像的能力，甚至在多步采样中表现更佳。 但 DDDM 中使用的伪 LPIPS (Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity) 损失函数引起了评估偏差的担忧。 uDDDM 旨在克服这些限制，通过以下方式改进现有技术：. **概率流 ODE (Probability Flow ODE, PF ODE)**: 扩散模型的目标是学习数据的分布。 VP 和 VE 模型都基于随机微分方程 (Stochastic Differential Equations, SDEs)。 将 SDE 转化为 ODE 可以获得更高效的采样。在 VP 和 VE 中, 使用PF ODE 来描述从噪声到数据的演化过程。. **统一表示:** 论文的核心贡献之一是将 VP 和 VE 模型的 PF ODE 统一到一个框架中。 这通过定义一个通用的函数 `h(x0, xt, t)` 来实现，该函数根据当前是 VP 还是 VE 模型而采用不同的形式。. `h(x0, xt, t) = (dσ^2_t/dt) * ∇xt log pt(xt)`. `h(x0, xt, t) = 1/2 * β(t) * [xt - ∇xt log qt(xt)]`. 这里的 `x0` 是原始数据，`xt` 是在时间 `t` 的噪声数据，`σ_t` 是 VE 模型中时间 `t` 的噪声尺度，`β(t)` 是 VP 模型中时间 `t` 的方差计划函数。. **模型预测:** uDDDM 使用神经网络 `fθ(x0, xt, t)` 来预测 PF ODE 的解，从而恢复原始数据 `x0`。 为了提高训练的稳定性，VE 模型的预测函数被重写为 `f(x0, xt, t) = κ(σt)xt + (1 - κ(σt)) * [xt - (1/(1 - κ(σt))) ∫h(x0, xs, s) ds]`， 其中 `κ(σt)` 是一个缩放因子，用于平衡当前状态 `xt` 和积分项的贡献。 常用的 κ(σt) 是`κ(σt) = σdata/(σt+σdata)` 或者 `κ(σt) = σ^2data/(σ^2t +σ^2data)`。 论文中使用 `κ(σt) = σmin/σt`。. `f(x0, xt, t) = κ(σt)xt + (1 - κ(σt)) * [xt - (1/(1 - κ(σt))) ∫h(x0, xs, s) ds]`. `κ(σt) = σdata/(σt+σdata)`. `κ(σt) = σ^2data/(σ^2t +σ^2data)`. **迭代细化:** 通过迭代的方式不断改进对 `x0` 的估计，使用更新方程 `x0^(n+1) = fθ(x0^n, xt, t)`。. `x0^(n+1) = fθ(x0^n, xt, t)`. `L(n)uDDDM(θ) = 1/(n+1) * L(n)Guide(θ) + (1 - 1/(n+1)) * L(n)Iter(θ)`. `L(n)Guide(θ) = E[d(fθ(x0^n, xt, t), x0)]`. `L(n)Iter(θ) = E[d(fθ(x0^n, xt, t), x0^n)]`. `d(x, y) = √(||x - y||^2 + c^2) - c`. ## 免费AI PDF查看器 革新您的论文阅读方式. / CEO Younghyun Chung / Business Registration Number 271-86-02206. 6F, 11-8 Teheran-ro 77-gil, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea, 06159.
